subject.title: feat(skills): declarative cron-trigger metadata in SKILL.md frontmatter

question: Should OpenClaw allow SKILL.md metadata to declare autonomous scheduled or event-triggered agent runs, and if so under which permission and approval model?
rationale: The requested field is not just display metadata: it could turn installed skill content into future autonomous execution, so maintainers must choose the product and security boundary before a safe implementation exists.

options.title: Design a permissioned core contract
options.body: Add a reviewed metadata namespace plus explicit operator approval, provenance, revocation, audit state, and scheduler/event integration before accepting skill-declared triggers.

options.title: Keep scheduling explicit
options.body: Do not let SKILL.md register jobs; document explicit cron jobs or standing orders as the supported path and close or narrow this request.

options.title: Defer to plugin/ClawHub APIs
options.body: Expose only the missing generic plugin or ClawHub indexing hooks, leaving skill packages to declare intent without core auto-registration.

recommendation.title: Design a permissioned core contract
recommendation.body: Add a reviewed metadata namespace plus explicit operator approval, provenance, revocation, audit state, and scheduler/event integration before accepting skill-declared triggers.

likelyOwner.reason: The current blame and sampled history place the central skill metadata, prompt, cron snapshot, and cron scheduler surfaces under recent work by this owner candidate.
